name: feast

attributes.attribute: followed the pattern of the other Celtic lands
was a great and public ceremonial act
marked shared identity and social bonds
joined living people and the powers of the land

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text:
A feast was a great ceremonial activity in ancient Celtic society. It helped a people show who they were and how they stood with their neighbors. The feast was a marker of shared identity. Scholars treat the feast as tricky evidence. It comes from two different kinds of source. The pre-Christian burials at Hallstatt and La Tene in mainland Europe leave no written word. The first tales of Ireland and Wales are full of imagination. It is a mistake to explain one kind of fact by the other. The two groups may seem more alike than they really are.

The archaeology is strong. In the early Iron Age the people of west-central Europe met the lands around the Mediterranean. They borrowed the custom of the drinking meeting, which the Greeks called the symposium. They took such objects as sieves and flagons for pouring wine. The decorated style of La Tene appears on many a metal drinking cup. Scholars read these as the gear of the noble feast. Fine cups, serving tools, food and drink form the heart of the rich graves of the Hallstatt and La Tene ages. Such finds appear from Gaul to central Europe to Britain. Good examples are the graves at Hochdorf, Vix, Reinheim and the princely series. In earlier Gaul people sometimes killed an animal and ate its meat at the same feast. Enclosed yards and halls may have held a common ritual meal. In Ireland the animal bones and the plan of the royal settlement hint at a feast at the turn of the season.

The Greek and Roman writers record feasts in sharp detail. There is the story of the great feast of a Gaulish chief. The host set the time for the praise poets, and the singers were rewarded with cups of gold. Another chief kept the feast going at great halls for a full year. At many feasts the warriors competed in strong tests, and a brave man offered his neck to the blade. One old writer says that a host secretly poisoned the guests from a distant land. The founding tale of a Greek city in Gaul is told as the story of men who came to a royal marriage feast in the heart of the Gaulish land.

The tradition of Ireland gives the fullest record. The rules for the table of a king are set out in a wise text from the ninth century. The old word for a royal feast in Irish carried the deeper sense of a joining. It was a rite of union, like the making of a marriage or the fixing of a true king. Later the word came to mean any great feast. The feast of Tara was the rite that drew the power of the land to a whole king. The people linked the first night of a king with union with the goddess of the land. A number of the old tales end at a feast. In them heroic men matched their force and courage at the table, and the strongest claimed the best joint of the meat. The word for the feast and its one root are common to every land of the Celtic tongue. In this way the feast joined the living people of the tribe with the older powers of the land.

okr.objective: The feast was a central Celtic rite that joined human groups with the powers of the land.
